 The Golden State Warriors have to feel like they're in a somewhat decent position to go out and make a move at the moment, specifically with how they've looked on both sides of the basketball.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement If the Warriors had come out this season and struggled at a somewhat high level throughout the first two weeks of the season, that would be a different story. Instead, the Warriors have played decent basketball, and as a result, they're likely going to make some additions at this year's trade deadline and even before that.
 There's an obvious need for some more size in Golden State, especially with Kristaps Porzingis not expected to be on the roster for much longer, and even if he is, he's not expected to play due to a health concern.
 The Warriors will have to get creative in who they want to add, but the latest report suggests that they have their eyes set on a former lottery pick in Jalen Smith, who is now with the Chicago Bulls .
 "The Warriors have called Chicago, sources say, because the Bulls theoretically offer a potential short-term answer: Jalen Smith. The 26-year-old has some floor-spacing ability and is earning roughly half of what Porziņģis is making this season at $9.4 million on the final season of a three-year, $27 million contract," Jake Fischer wrote, H/T Hoops Hype .
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Smith is a decent player in his own right, but he's not going to be somebody who comes in and averages 20-plus points per night for the Warriors.
 This is a player who can give them 15 to 20 minutes per game of average play, and that might be all Golden State needs at the center position for now. Having Porzingis obviously would have been the better outcome, but that doesn't look to be a realistic possibility for the Warriors any longer.
